title: Exploring the role of HNF1B in the pathogenesis of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD): an integrative bioinformatics study.
authors: Cao, Wenlong; Yao, Ye; Chen, Yiwen; Wang, Yuqin; Xiong, Jing
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过生物信息学分析HNF1B在ADPKD中的表达及上游转录因子预测，但核心是疾病机制而非TF-DNA互作建模，方法以数据库预测和分子对接为主，缺乏AI或物理模拟的深度建模。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Hepatocyte nuclear factor 1 beta (HNF1beta) is crucial for renal tubule development, and its mutation causes renal cysts. However, its role in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) remains unclear. This study explored the mechanism of hepatocyte nuclear factor 1-beta gene (HNF1B) in ADPKD using integrative bioinformatics analysis. METHODS: HNF1B expression was evaluated in ADPKD transcriptome datasets and validated via immunofluorescence in a 3D Madin-Darby canine kidney cell cyst model cultured over a 12-day timeframe (analyzed on days 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12). Based on HNF1B median expression, ADPKD tissues were divided into high- and low-expression groups for differential and enrichment analyses. Upstream transcription factors and binding sites were predicted using UCSC and JASPAR databases. Finally, cMAP and L1000FWD were used to screen therapeutic small molecules targeting HNF1beta, followed by molecular docking. RESULTS: HNF1B was significantly downregulated in ADPKD tissues (p = 0.017) and correlated with cyst progression (p < 0.001), which was consistent with the 3D model findings (p < 0.001). Low HNF1B expression was associated with transcriptomic signatures reflecting activation of the wingless-related integration site (Wnt) and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-beta) pathways and inhibition of the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) pathway. POU3F3, HNF4A, and TFAP2B were identified as potential upstream transcription factors. Mocetinostat (binding energy = -8.2 kcal/mol) and wortmannin (binding energy = -7.7 kcal/mol) showed stable binding to HNF1beta. CONCLUSION: HNF1B expression is significantly negatively correlated with cyst progression, suggesting a potential protective role in ADPKD, and its downregulation associates with pathways driving cyst progression.
abstract_zh: 目的：肝细胞核因子1β（HNF1beta）对肾小管发育至关重要，其突变可导致肾囊肿。然而，其在常染色体显性多囊肾病（ADPKD）中的作用仍不清楚。本研究通过整合生物信息学分析探讨了肝细胞核因子1-β基因（HNF1B）在ADPKD中的机制。方法：在ADPKD转录组数据集中评估HNF1B表达，并通过免疫荧光在12天时间框架内（在第4、6、8、10和12天分析）培养的3D Madin-Darby犬肾细胞囊肿模型中进行验证。基于HNF1B中位表达，将ADPKD组织分为高表达组和低表达组，进行差异分析和富集分析。使用UCSC和JASPAR数据库预测上游转录因子及其结合位点。最后，使用cMAP和L1000FWD筛选靶向HNF1beta的治疗性小分子，随后进行分子对接。结果：HNF1B在ADPKD组织中显著下调（p = 0.017），并与囊肿进展相关（p < 0.001），这与3D模型结果一致（p < 0.001）。低HNF1B表达与反映无翼相关整合位点（Wnt）和转化生长因子-β（TGF-beta）通路激活以及过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体（PPAR）通路抑制的转录组特征相关。POU3F3、HNF4A和TFAP2B被鉴定为潜在的上游转录因子。Mocetinostat（结合能 = -8.2 kcal/mol）和wortmannin（结合能 = -7.7 kcal/mol）显示出与HNF1beta的稳定结合。结论：HNF1B表达与囊肿进展显著负相关，提示其在ADPKD中可能具有保护作用，其下调与驱动囊肿进展的通路相关。
